# Implement version read + dimmed right-aligned header display

## Summary
Read the plugin version at runtime from `packages/herdr/package.json` and render it as a dimmed, right-aligned `v<version>` suffix in the work item selection list header, without disturbing the left-aligned title.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A runtime helper reads the plugin version from `packages/herdr/package.json` (JSON parse via `readFileSync`, following the `shortcut-config.ts` pattern); when the file is missing or unparseable it falls back gracefully (e.g. `'?'` or omit) without throwing.
- The list-mode header renders `v<version>` right-aligned to `cols` (visible-width padding computed with ANSI codes stripped before padding), dimmed via `ANSI.dim`, matching the `[auto-refresh on]` treatment; the left-aligned `Work Items — N item(s)` title is unchanged.
- The version is read at runtime from the manifest, not hardcoded in the renderer (stays in sync with the manifest version).
- On narrow panes where the suffix would overlap the title, the suffix is dropped or truncated (guard on `cols`) — no layout breakage, no overflow beyond the pane width.
- Full project test suite passes with the new changes, including the header version tests (F1).

## Minimal Implementation
- Add a small version-read helper in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (or a sibling module) using the `readFileSync`/`dirname` pattern from `shortcut-config.ts`, with a safe fallback.
- In the list-mode header renderer (near line ~1585): compute the header's visible width, pad to `cols`, and append the dimmed `v<version>` suffix right-aligned; reuse `truncateLine`/visible-length logic; guard on `cols` for narrow panes.
- Keep the renderer testable via the existing `readFile`-style injection seam where practical.

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: header version rendering tests (F1) — test-first ordering.

## Deliverables
- Updated `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`; version helper; no change to `packages/herdr/package.json` (version source only).

# Intake Brief: Herdr audit dispatch — deepen per-window batch when the in_review queue is deep (WL-0MVEDM8OT007WDRS)

## Headline

Make the herdr downtime dispatcher drain a deep `completed`/`in_review` backlog faster by allowing **sequential** audit dispatches to continue within one continuous idle window (up to a small cap) whenever the audit-eligible queue depth reaches `browseItemCount`. Concurrency safety is unchanged: at most one audit is ever active, and every dispatch still passes the idle-duration gate, the ≥2 free-slot minimum, the host-wide audit marker and the per-worklog single-flight.

## Problem statement

The downtime dispatcher currently requires a fresh full idle period after **every** successful dispatch (`tracker.record(false)` in the worker tick), and the host-wide active-audit marker (WL-0MUIVE0YG000UVIA) blocks a second audit dispatch while one is running. Under sustained agent traffic, idle windows are rare, so the audit tier drains at roughly one item per idle window even when the `completed`/`in_review` queue is dozens of items deep. The audit skill can already process several items per seeded run (batch drain, SA-0MTG5TP5Z008QBL5), but herdr only ever seeds a single-item `/skill:audit <id>` dispatch.

## Users

- **Producer / sprint lead** — wants the review queue to drain during idle compute so items reach release sooner.
  - *User story:* As a producer, when the review queue is deeper than my sprint window, I want the dispatcher to use one idle window for several audits (one after another) instead of one audit per window, so the backlog drains days faster without any extra LLM load.
- **Downtime dispatcher operator** — wants predictable, observable batching that never breaks the safety gates or the host-wide audit slot.
  - *User story:* As an operator, when the queue is shallow I want exactly today's behaviour, and when batching is active I want to see why each extra audit was (or was not) dispatched in the decision log.
- **Audit-tier agents** — must keep receiving one work item per dispatch and never see a duplicate or concurrent audit.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Depth-aware batching: an audit-eligible depth at or above `browseItemCount` with `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_BATCH_MAX` above 1 allows distinct audit continuations inside one idle window until the cap or the depth drop.

  Details: **Depth-aware audit batching (opt-in by depth).** When the audit-eligible backlog — root `completed`/`in_review` items that `classifyItemForDispatch` maps to `audit` (i.e. without a fresh audit and not held) — is at least `browseItemCount`, and `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_BATCH_MAX` (default 2, clamped, `1` = legacy/off) is greater than 1, the dispatcher may continue dispatching distinct audit targets within the same continuous idle window until the cap is reached or the depth drops below the threshold. When the depth is below the threshold, behaviour is unchanged: one dispatch per window and a fresh idle period is required before the next.

- Sequential single-audit safety: every continuation re-checks the idle-duration gate, `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS = 2`, proxy contention, code freeze, the active-audit markers and single-flight — no gate is relaxed, only the post-dispatch idle reset is deferred.

  Details: **Sequential single-audit safety.** The batch continuation never starts a second audit while one is active: it waits for the previous audit's host-wide/per-worklog marker to be released, and re-checks — on every continuation — the continuous idle-duration gate, `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS = 2`, proxy contention (`contention_queue_depth == 0`), the code-freeze marker, the machine-wide active-audit marker and the per-worklog single-flight. No gate is relaxed or bypassed; only the post-dispatch "require a fresh full idle period" reset is deferred for an audit-batch continuation.

- No duplicate or re-dispatched items: each continuation selects a distinct item through the existing classification and dispatched-marker exclusions, and any non-`dispatched` outcome ends the batch.

  Details: **No duplicate or re-dispatched items.** Each continuation selects a distinct item through the existing classification and dispatched-marker exclusions (audit id-guard, staleness-aware marker release, attempt budget, freshness/recency). A failed CAS claim, claim rollback, spawn failure, or any non-`dispatched` outcome ends the current batch rather than skipping to another target.

- Coordination-mode compatibility: the leader sources continuation targets from its own Herdr head without releasing leadership mid-batch, and hands off leadership once at batch end.

  Details: **Coordination-mode compatibility.** On the production coordination path the leader sources continuation targets from its own Herdr head (bounded window extension, same ranking path) without releasing leadership mid-batch; leadership hand-off still occurs once after the batch ends when the fallback was used. When the depth drops below threshold or the cap is reached, normal single-dispatch behaviour resumes immediately.

- Observability: every batch decision is recorded in the downtime decision log with a distinct reason token (`audit-batch-continue` and the existing held/blocked tokens) including depth, cap and remaining; rate limiting is unchanged.

  Details: **Observability.** Every batch decision is recorded in the existing downtime decision log with a distinct reason token (e.g. `audit-batch-continue`, and the existing tokens for held/blocked continuations), including depth, cap and remaining count. Existing reason tokens and rate limiting are unchanged.

- Test coverage in the herdr package: shallow depth keeps the single-dispatch idle reset; depth at or above `browseItemCount` with `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_BATCH_MAX = N` yields N sequential audits in one idle window; idle gates, the active-audit marker, the cap, the depth drop and dispatched-marker exclusion are asserted.

  Details: **Test coverage (herdr package).** Unit tests assert: (a) shallow depth keeps today's single-dispatch behaviour including the idle-tracker reset; (b) depth ≥ `browseItemCount` with `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_BATCH_MAX = N` produces N sequential audit dispatches within one idle window; (c) an unsatisfied idle-duration gate (and sub-2 free slots) blocks all dispatch, including continuations; (d) the host-wide/per-worklog active-audit marker blocks a concurrent continuation, and continuation proceeds only after release; (e) the cap and the depth-drop are respected; (f) dispatched-marker exclusion prevents the same item being selected twice.

- Documentation: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `packages/herdr/README.md` and the settings reference document the new setting, the activation rule, the sequential safety invariants and the new decision tokens.

  Details: **Documentation.** `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `packages/herdr/README.md` and the settings reference document the new setting, the activation rule, the sequential safety invariants and the new decision tokens. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

- Full suite: the full project test suite passes with the new changes, at minimum the full herdr package suite.

  Details: **Full suite.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (at minimum the full herdr package suite).

## Constraints

- Keep the strict idle-duration gate and `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS = 2` for every dispatch: reserve at least one local slot, and never fan out concurrent audits.
- The host-wide single-audit contract (WL-0MUIVE0YG000UVIA) remains the hard concurrency cap; this item changes only *cadence within one idle window*, never audit concurrency.
- Must not destabilise leader election/lease (5-minute TTL), coordination check-ins, pruning, fail-closed lookups, the review-queue gate, or the coordination offer path.
- Reuse `browseItemCount` (`readReviewQueueGate` / `resolveSprintViewWindow`) as the single "deep queue" threshold; do not add a second depth definition.
- The new setting is `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_BATCH_MAX` (settings key `downtimeAuditBatchMax`), default `2`, clamped to a safe range; `1` disables batching and restores legacy behaviour.
- No SorraAgents/audit-skill changes: the audit skill's own batch drain remains the mechanism that processes multiple items after a dispatch; herdr only decides how many audit panes to seed per window.
- Do not change the legacy `dispatchDowntimeWork` tier chain's semantics beyond the shared continuation logic; the production path is coordination mode.
- **Out of scope:** relaxing the host-wide single-audit marker, changing `AUDIT_BATCH_MAX_ITEMS`/`AUDIT_BATCH_TIMEOUT` in SorraAgents, and any non-audit batching.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `dispatchDowntimeWork` consumes the Herdr list head and applies safety gates as sequential filters; `dispatchFromCoordination` (leader) dispatches at most one offer per tick and only reads its own extended head as a fallback when nothing in the offer list is dispatchable; the worker `tick()` calls `tracker.record(false)` / `perSlotTracker.record([])` after a successful dispatch, which is the per-window reset.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `readReviewQueueGate` already measures the root-only `completed`/`in_review` count against `browseItemCount` (`resolveSprintViewWindow`), and `classifyItemForDispatch` already decides whether an item is an audit candidate, including freshness/recency.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `getActiveAudit` checks the machine-wide `~/.herdr/downtime/active-audit` marker before the per-worklog dispatch-log marker; `recordDispatch` writes both, `recordPaneClose`/`recordDispatchFailure` release them.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `createDowntimeDeps` wires the Herdr head, `fetchItem`, `getActiveAudit`, dispatch markers and the pane-close hooks.
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — downtime settings plumbing, defaults and clamping (the new `downtimeAuditBatchMax` follows the same pattern).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.audit-tier.test.ts`, `downtime-worker.dispatch.test.ts`, `downtime-worker.orchestrator.test.ts`, `coordination-dispatch.test.ts` — where the existing single-dispatch and audit-tier behaviour is asserted.

## Desired change

1. Add a bounded, depth-derived batch mode: compute the audit-eligible depth from the already-fetched Herdr head (root `completed`/`in_review` items are mandatory in the head), activate only when `depth >= browseItemCount` and `downtimeAuditBatchMax > 1`, and expose the remaining budget to the dispatch path.
2. In `tick()`, replace the unconditional post-dispatch idle reset with a conditional one: on a successful **audit** dispatch in active batch mode with budget remaining, keep the idle tracker armed for an audit continuation (subject to a fresh per-tick idle/slot/contention re-check); for every other dispatch, or when the budget/threshold no longer applies, preserve today's reset exactly.
3. In `dispatchFromCoordination`, allow the leader to source a continuation audit target from its own head extension after a successful batch-eligible audit dispatch, instead of only after total offer-list exhaustion; defer the own-backlog leadership hand-off until the batch ends.
4. Add `downtimeAuditBatchMax` to settings (default 2, clamped, 1 = off) and thread it through `DowntimeWorkerConfig` and the dispatch options.
5. Record `audit-batch-continue` (and held variants) in the decision log, with depth/cap/remaining metadata, at the existing rate limit.
6. Add the unit tests listed in AC6 and update the dispatcher docs/README.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — batch depth computation, continuation budget, conditional idle reset, leader continuation path, decision-log token.
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — `downtimeAuditBatchMax` default, parsing and clamping.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — thread the new setting into `createDowntimeWorker`/dispatch config.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.audit-tier.test.ts` — depth-aware batch activation, cap and marker/single-flight safety tests.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch.test.ts` — shallow-depth regression and idle-reset behaviour.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.orchestrator.test.ts` — worker-loop continuation, idle gate blocking, leadership hand-off timing.
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.test.ts` — leader own-head continuation and distinct-target guarantees.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.settings.test.ts` — setting default/clamp coverage.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — activation rule, sequential safety invariants, decision tokens.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — operator-facing description of the new setting.

## Related work

- WL-0MT3PHW4I002SNOV — active-audit single-flight (per-worklog); preserved per item, not relaxed.
- WL-0MUIVE0YG000UVIA — host-wide audit serialisation; remains the hard concurrency cap.
- WL-0MT32F90V008UAD2 — per-tier free-slot minimums (audit needs 2); reused unchanged.
- WL-0MST3OJ8S0001ROL — downtime dispatcher leader election and coordination.
- WL-0MUU4XFU90008E24 — own-backlog fallback relinquishes leadership; must be deferred to batch end.
- WL-0MUNS8X97007C9H9 — sprint-view-only dispatch window (`browseItemCount` head).
- WL-0MT47BQAT00375VB — active-audit detection and audit-tier skip (per-worklog marker).
- WL-0MT2UQWOR007CYY9 — review-queue depth gate (same `browseItemCount` signal).
- WL-0MTTSWC1X005P4VD — review-queue gate rewiring (neutral `review-queue-hold`).
- SA-0MTG5TP5Z008QBL5 (SorraAgents) — audit batch drain that consumes the seeded window.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: non-audit tiers could be starved** while a batch continues. Mitigation: batching applies only to audit dispatches and only while `depth >= browseItemCount`; as soon as no audit candidate remains, the normal tier/ranking resumes.
- **Risk: leadership hand-off logic regressed.** The existing own-backlog dispatch releases leadership immediately; deferring it for a batch could strand the leader if the batch never ends. Mitigation: release at batch end, on any failed continuation, and on the next tick when the cap/depth condition no longer holds; cover with an orchestrator test.
- **Risk: the idle-reset change leaks into other kinds.** Mitigation: scope the conditional reset to the audit-batch continuation flag only; add a regression test asserting non-audit dispatch still resets the tracker.
- **Risk: extra `wl` reads per tick hurt latency.** Mitigation: derive depth from the already-fetched head; no new subprocess in the common path.
- **Risk: a continuation starts during a code freeze or after the queue drops.** Mitigation: re-read the freeze marker and re-compute depth on every continuation tick; any frozen/ambiguous state or depth < threshold simply ends the batch and restores normal behaviour.
- **Assumption:** `completed`/`in_review` root items are mandatory-always in the Herdr head, so the head is a complete depth source up to `browseItemCount` and beyond (the existing window extension covers overflow).
- **Assumption:** the host-wide marker is released when the audit pane closes (`recordPaneClose`) or a spawn fails, so a continuation can start promptly without weakening the marker's stale window.
- **Assumption:** a sequential audit batch is acceptable to the audit runner's host-wide `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY=1` slot because at most one audit pane is active at a time.
- **Scope-creep risk:** relaxing host-wide serialisation (option B) or changing `AUDIT_BATCH_MAX_ITEMS` (option C) is explicitly out of scope; if either becomes necessary it should be raised as a separate work item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (mechanism):** How should "more than one audit per window" work — (A) keep exactly one active audit and continue sequentially within a continuous idle window, (B) dispatch N audit panes in one tick, or (C) seed the audit skill's batch queue with N ids?
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply):** **(A)** — keep exactly one active audit; when depth ≥ threshold, skip the fresh-idle-period reset so the next audit dispatches once the previous audit pane closes and slots are idle again.
  - **Evidence:** host-wide active-audit marker semantics (`docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` § Host-wide audit serialisation) and `tick()`'s post-dispatch `tracker.record(false)`.
- **Q2 (threshold):** Reuse `browseItemCount` or add a dedicated threshold?
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply):** **Reuse `browseItemCount`** as the single deep-queue signal; add only the small cap `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_BATCH_MAX` (default 2).
  - **Evidence:** `readReviewQueueGate`/`resolveSprintViewWindow` already define "deep" for the review-queue gate.
- **Q3 (second target source):** Where should the extra audit target(s) come from in coordination mode?
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply):** **(A)** the leader re-reads its own Herdr head after the first dispatch (extend the existing own-backlog fallback).
  - **Evidence:** `dispatchFromCoordination`'s own-backlog fallback (`getHerdrListHead` + `fetchExtendedHerdrItems`) and WL-0MUU4XFU90008E24.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MSK9TUCA00206M7** – RCA: no downtime dispatch overnight despite continuous idle-window status polling (~16 polls/min, 7h idle) (completed)
- **WL-0MSKUG2WI004CBW3** – Check dispatch logs/leases on 192.168.0.191 filesystem (completed)
- **WL-0MRMCO4VB009HIJL** – Tests: getChordByPrefix and arbitrary-depth dispatch (completed)

# Decompose the `downtime-worker.ts` god class

**File:** `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` (8,105 lines, 174 exported symbols, 23 logical sections)

## Problem statement

`downtime-worker.ts` has grown into a single 8,105-line module that carries the
entire downtime-dispatch subsystem: constants, public types, idle detection,
the local-status poller, dispatchability gates, the Herdr list-head dispatch
pipeline, leader-election coordination, pane spawning and lifecycle, the worker
tick orchestrator, wl-output parsers, per-tier selection, settings clamps and
round-robin helpers. Navigating, reviewing and safely changing any one concern
requires holding the whole file in view, so every dispatch change carries
avoidable regression risk.

## Users

- **Downtime-dispatch maintainers (agents and humans)** need to change one
  concern (e.g. a gate, a tier parser, the spawn path) without reasoning about
  8,000 unrelated lines.
- **Reviewers/auditors** need to review a focused diff where the blast radius of
  a change is legible from the touched module.
- **Future agents implementing dispatch work items** need small, named modules
  they can locate with a file search instead of reading a monolith.

Example user stories:

- As an agent implementing a dispatch-gate change, I want the gate logic in a
  dedicated module so that I can modify it without re-reading the whole worker.
- As a reviewer, I want a split diff to be attributable to a single concern so
  that I can verify it against its own tests.
- As a maintainer, I want each module under 1,000 lines so that the file is
  readable in a single pass.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No file exceeds 1,000 lines.** After the change, `wc -l` reports ≤1,000 for
   `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` (now a thin barrel) and for every
   module created by the split.
2. **Public surface preserved — used symbols only.** Every symbol currently
   imported from `./downtime-worker.js` by another module remains exported from
   that exact path with identical types and values, so the 33 importing files
   compile with no import-path edits. The barrel re-exports **only symbols that
   are actually used** by consumers; symbols that nothing outside the split
   modules imports are internal and need not be re-exported (producer decision
   on Q2).
3. **Behaviour-preserving, move-only refactor.** No functional or logic change;
   no test file is modified (not its import paths, fixtures or assertions), and
   all 15 `downtime-worker.*` test suites plus the whole `packages/herdr` suite
   pass unchanged.
4. **No new circular imports.** Extracted modules import only from concrete
   sibling modules, never from the `downtime-worker.js` barrel; the dependency
   check reports no new cycles and does not extend the pre-existing
   `stalled-work ↔ downtime-worker` type-only cycle into runtime values.
5. **Single-flight state remains singular.** The module-level mutable
   `dispatchInFlightCount` (current line 2523) lives in exactly one module and
   is not duplicated by the split, so per-process dispatch single-flight
   semantics are unchanged.
6. **Responsibility documented per module.** Each new module carries a
   module-level doc comment stating its single responsibility, and the existing
   provenance comments (work-item ids, section banners) move with their code so
   traceability is preserved.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
8. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Move-only.** Relocate code and update imports; do not refactor logic,
  rename public symbols, or change behaviour.
- **Barrel compatibility.** 33 files import from `./downtime-worker.js`,
  including 15 `downtime-worker.*` test suites (~15,000 test lines) and the
  production consumers `index.ts`, `settings.ts`, `ship-guard.ts`,
  `fetcher.ts`, `stalled-work.ts`, `worklist.ts`, plus 11 other test files.
  The barrel preserves that contract.
- **Sequenced, tree-green landing.** Extract leaf modules first (constants,
  types, clamps/parsers) and work inwards, so each merged step leaves the build
  and the full suite green.
- **No new runtime dependencies**, no test-file rewrites, no changes to the wl
  CLI contract or dispatch behaviour.
- **Scope boundary.** The item targets `downtime-worker.ts`; the other
  `packages/herdr` files above 1,000 lines are explicitly out of scope (see
  Risks — scope creep).

## Existing state

`downtime-worker.ts` is 8,105 lines. Its section inventory (line ranges from the
current `dev` checkout) is:

| # | Section | Lines | Size |
|---|---------|-------|------|
| 1 | Constants | 204–616 | 413 |
| 2 | Types | 617–709 | 93 |
| 3 | Idle detection | 710–862 | 153 |
| 4 | Idle-duration tracker | 863–902 | 40 |
| 5 | Per-slot idle tracker | 903–964 | 62 |
| 6 | Poller | 965–1248 | 284 |
| 7 | Dispatch (types + claim/result helpers) | 1249–2538 | 1,290 |
| 8 | Review-queue depth gate | 2539–2724 | 186 |
| 9 | Critical-only dispatch-window escape hatch | 2725–2776 | 52 |
| 10 | Herdr list-head filter dispatcher | 2777–3695 | 919 |
| 11 | Leader-election coordination dispatch | 3696–5614 | 1,919 |
| 12 | Pane-lifecycle monitor | 5615–5773 | 159 |
| 13 | Worker orchestrator | 5774–6932 | 1,159 |
| 14 | Blocked-questions prompt | 6933–6985 | 53 |
| 15 | Wiring helpers | 6986–7089 | 104 |
| 16 | Rotation-aware selection | 7090–7147 | 58 |
| 17 | Audit-tier selection | 7148–7307 | 160 |
| 18 | Implement-tier selection | 7308–7471 | 164 |
| 19 | Plan/intake selection | 7472–7510 | 39 |
| 20 | Critical-first selection | 7511–7804 | 294 |
| 21 | Dependency frontier resolution | 7805–7913 | 109 |
| 22 | Settings clamps | 7914–8034 | 121 |
| 23 | Round-robin helpers | 8035–8105 | 71 |

Relevant structural facts discovered during intake:

- **Module-level mutable state:** `let dispatchInFlightCount = 0` (line 2523)
  backs the per-process dispatch-pipeline single-flight gate.
- **Pre-existing coupling:** `stalled-work.ts` imports
  `parseDepListBlockersOutput`, `isAttemptBudgetExhausted`, `paneLabelItemId`
  and several types from `./downtime-worker.js`, while `downtime-worker.ts`
  imports `StalledPaneCandidate`, `StalledResumeOutcome` and `StalledScanOptions`
  types from `./stalled-work.js` — an existing type-only cycle that the split
  must not turn into a runtime cycle.
- **Precedent:** [WL-0MQJK4UJD0028IRO](../../../../.worklog) decomposed the
  2,584-line `src/database.ts` god class under ACs requiring an unchanged public
  API, tests passing without modification, and ≤500 lines per new module.

## Desired change

Reduce `downtime-worker.ts` to a thin re-export barrel and move its contents
into cohesive sibling modules, each well under 1,000 lines. A starting
decomposition (boundaries are an implementation decision, subject to the
constraints above):

| New module | Responsibility | Approx. size |
|---|---|---|
| `downtime-worker.constants.ts` | Tuning constants, floors/maxima, `decisionHeaderToken` | ~420 |
| `downtime-worker.types.ts` | Exported interfaces and unions (`LlamaStatus`, candidates, claim/result types, config, worker) | ~700 |
| `downtime-worker.idle.ts` | Idle detection, idle-duration tracker, per-slot tracker | ~255 |
| `downtime-worker.poller.ts` | `parseLlamaStatus`, `fetchLocalStatus`, `createDowntimePoller` | ~284 |
| `downtime-worker.gates.ts` | Soft-delete/assignee holds, review-queue depth gate, audit batch status, `classifyItemForDispatch`, attempt budget, critical-only escape hatch | ~480 |

# Reduce time to run tests

**Headline:** Identify and eliminate redundant or slow tests across the vitest and pytest suites so the canonical suite (tests/cli + tests/unit) drops from ~8.5–12.7 minutes to ~6 minutes or less (≥30% wall-clock reduction), without meaningful coverage loss.

## Problem statement

Running the project's test suite takes a very long time. The canonical suite (`tests/cli` + `tests/unit`, per `.pi/test-config.json`) recently takes **486–730 s for `tests/cli` alone** plus **22–28 s for `tests/unit`** (test-skill run cache, 2026-10-16→20), and the full vitest suite aggregates **~2434 s of test time across 8281 tests** (test-timings.json, 2026-10-20). The top 12 test files consume over 50% of aggregate runtime, and a single test (`read-cache-spawn-reduction`, a 6-pane simulation) takes **203 s**. Every implement/test/audit gate pays this cost, slowing agent and human delivery loops.

## Users

- **Primary:** Maintainers and agents running the test suite repeatedly for implement/test/audit gates and CI.
- **Secondary:** Contributors who need fast feedback on changed scope.

**User stories:**
- As a maintainer running the full suite, I want slow or redundant tests removed/optimised so each gate run is materially faster.
- As an agent on the test gate, I want the canonical suite to complete in minutes, not 10+ minutes, so I can iterate quickly.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Baseline recorded:** A baseline is captured on a consistent (idle-ish) host using the canonical commands (`npm --silent test -- tests/cli`, `npm --silent test -- tests/unit`, plus full `npm --silent test`), with per-test timings produced via `npm run test:timings`; the top-20 slowest tests are identified and listed in a comment on the work item.
2. **Measurable reduction:** The canonical suite wall-clock (tests/cli + tests/unit on the same host) is reduced by **≥30%** versus the recorded baseline.
3. **Per-test triage:** Every test ≥5 s is triaged — mocked/stubbed external dependency, moved to an integration-only/long-run location, or retained with a documented justification comment. No test is silently ignored.
4. **Redundancy removal:** Redundant, duplicated, or dead tests are removed with each removal accounted for (coverage preserved or explicitly migrated) in work-item comments; no meaningful coverage loss.
5. **Python suite included:** pytest tests (`tests/conftest.py`, `tests/test_*.py`) are measured and included in the same triage; slow python tests are optimised or justified.
6. **Green gate:** The full project test suite passes with the changes; a regression guard prevents reintroduction of a known worst offender if feasible.
7. **Docs updated:** All related documentation updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md`, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- No change to test behaviour semantics without a documented, coverage-preserving reason.
- Keep changes localised to test code and test config (vitest.config.ts, CI scripts) unless a production optimisation is the proven cause of a slow test.
- Tests must remain deterministic; the suite must run green 3× under CI-like conditions without intermittent timeouts.
- Python tests: keep pytest suite fast; do not break the audit-log/prune plugin coverage they provide.

## Existing state

- **Frameworks:** Vitest (TS/JS, `tests/` + `packages/`) and pytest (Python, `tests/test_*.py`).
- **Canonical suite** (`.pi/test-config.json`): `npm --silent test -- tests/cli` + `npm --silent test -- tests/unit`.
- **Recent canonical runtimes** (test-skill cache, green runs): tests/cli 183–785 s (median ~450 s; current ~660 s), tests/unit 7–41 s (median ~15 s).
- **Full suite aggregate:** 2434 s across 8281 tests; top files: read-cache-spawn-reduction (203 s), sync-vs-mutation (163 s), read-cache-e2e (146 s), close-recursive (128 s), init (109 s), issue-management (96 s), issue-status (75 s), startup-import-budget (73 s), valid-json-output (69 s), entry-point-split (67 s), install-herdr tests (67 s), json-output-shape (63 s). Slowest single tests: 203 s read-cache spawn-reduction, 69 s startup-import-budget, 47 s entry-point-split, 42 s sync-integration-convergence, ~26 s read-cache-e2e variants, ~20 s github-push-synced-items, ~16 s sync-assignee-clear, 13.4 s herdr build-guard (tsc).
- **Known trends:** transform/import overhead grows with per-file isolation (downtime-worker split measured +146% transform, +267% import). CLI suite runtime approximately doubled between 2026-10-17 (~180–280 s) and 2026-10-19–20 (~486–730 s), coinciding with read-cache, sync, and startup-budget test additions.

## Desired change

- Produce and publish a timings baseline; triage the top offenders; remove redundant/dead tests (with coverage accounting); mock/stub external dependencies (spawned `wl` processes, real git syncs, heavy setup) where feasible; move long-running integration tests to a separate long-run/CI group; apply the same treatment to pytest.
- Target: canonical suite wall-clock reduced ≥30%.

## Key Files

- `scripts/test-timings.cjs` — per-test timing collector (`npm run test:timings`); extend/use for baseline capture.
- `test-timings.json` — generated timing report (gitignore'd artefact).
- `tests/cli/read-cache-spawn-reduction.test.ts` — 203 s 6-pane simulation test, #1 offender.
- `tests/cli/sync-vs-mutation.test.ts` — 163 s race-condition sync tests.
- `tests/cli/read-cache-e2e.test.ts` — 146 s e2e read-cache tests (timeout-flaky under load per WL-0MUDYZ0QR002RO40).
- `tests/cli/close-recursive.test.ts`, `tests/cli/init.test.ts`, `tests/cli/issue-management.test.ts`, `tests/cli/issue-status.test.ts`, `tests/cli/valid-json-output.test.ts`, `tests/cli/startup-import-budget.test.ts`, `tests/cli/entry-point-split.test.ts`, `tests/scripts/install-herdr.test.ts`, `tests/cli/json-output-shape.test.ts`, `tests/cli/sync-author-gate.test.ts`, `tests/cli/stats-by-type.test.ts`, `tests/cli/sync-integration-convergence.test.ts` — remaining top offenders.
- `tests/cli/cli-helpers.ts`, `tests/test-utils.js` — shared CLI test helpers (setup/teardown consolidation point).
- `vitest.config.ts`, `tests/ci-run.sh` — worker/parallelism configuration.
- `.pi/test-config.json` — canonical suite definition.
- `tests/conftest.py`, `tests/test_audit_runner_core.py`, `tests/test_install_audit_log_hygiene.py`, `tests/test_prune_audit_debug_logs.py` — pytest files for the python pass.
- `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` — baseline documentation to update.

## Related work

- WL-0MLB6RMQ0095SKKE — Refactor slow CLI tests (completed; prior slow-CLI effort, review its outcomes first).
- WL-0MLLHF9GX1VYY0H0 — Add per-test timing collector and report (completed; `npm run test:timings` tooling).
- WL-0MP14TVLV004U2B2 — Add per-test timings docs to README/tests.md (completed).
- WL-0MV4UZ6C4007XDGI — Legacy `test/` vs `tests/` deduplication (completed).
- WL-0MV4VTFYE0073POG — downtime-worker test-split runtime measurement (completed; documents per-file isolation overhead).
- WL-0MUDYZ0QR002RO40 — read-cache-e2e timeout flakiness (completed; fix folded into this optimisation where relevant).
- WL-0MVFNMSRW002FI6B — Investigate transient wl process CPU usage (in-progress; read-cache/startup test family).
- WL-0MSGAE35E001557V — Read-cache core module (completed; source of the read-cache e2e/spawn-reduction tests).
- WL-0MVFRRAXD001E7AN — Startup import-budget harness and baseline (completed; source of the 69 s startup-import-budget test).

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

1. Q: Current test run time? Have skills left logs? — A (producer, interactive): "I do not know, don't skills leave logs?" — Research: the test skill's per-repo run cache (`.worklog/cache/`) records every full-suite run. Recent canonical green runs: tests/cli 486–730 s, tests/unit 22–28 s → canonical ~510–760 s total. Full suite aggregates 2434 s test-time across 8281 tests (test-timings.json, 2026-10-20). Baseline accepted from skill logs.
2. Q: Scope (canonical/full/specific area)? — A: both — canonical and full suite; no specific area, "just aiming for faster."
3. Q: New work beyond prior slow-CLI refactor? — A: review the work done, look for additional improvement opportunities.
4. Q: Approach (remove / optimise / both / other)? — A: c — both remove redundant/dead tests and optimise slow tests.
5. Q: Python (pytest) tests in scope? — A: yes — tests/test_audit_runner_core.py, tests/test_install_audit_log_hygiene.py, tests/test_prune_audit_debug_logs.py, tests/conftest.py.

**Assumptions:** target ≥30% canonical wall-clock reduction vs recorded baseline (no explicit number supplied); timing is host-dependent so baseline must be re-measured on a consistent host before/after.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Host-load noise:** absolute timings are host/load-dependent (shared 16-core host); mitigations: measure baseline and post-change on the same host, use median of ≥3 runs, record load average.
- **Coverage loss on removal:** a removed test may carry unique coverage; mitigation: per-removal accounting (work-item comments), rely on full suite green + coverage review.
- **Flakiness from mocking:** replacing real git/process spawns with mocks can introduce false confidence; mitigation: keep at least one real integration test per subsystem, move to long-run group rather than delete.
- **Scope creep:** parallelisation, CI sharding, and test-infra rewrites are attractive but out of scope; record as linked follow-up work items, not this brief.
- **Recent runtime inflation correlates with read-cache/sync/startup test additions** (CLI suite ~2× Oct 17→Oct 20); a quick win may be reworking these to shared fixtures or fewer spawns, but assume nothing until the triage pass measures it.

## Problem statement (headline)

Every `wl` command spawns a fresh Node.js process that takes **0.6–1.7 s and 80–180 MB** just to boot (a bare `node -e ''` is 0.35 s / 58 MB): the CLI eagerly imports 40+ modules (commander, all ~35 command builders, plugins, runtime, `better-sqlite3`) before any command logic, and herdr panes + pi agents fire these one-shot processes continuously (30 s refresh ticks, 60 s `sync --if-idle` per pane, per-agent polls). Four concurrent `wl` processes were observed at 25–65 % CPU each — bursty, seconds-long, gone moments later. The shipped read-cache (WL-0MSAZQEQB008O7H3) cut *read work* (83 %) but deliberately left process spawning unchanged ("each invocation still spawns a wl process"). There is also an unbounded hygiene leak: `~/.cache/wl/state/` holds **216,228 one-file-per-worklog-dir counters (~890 MB, 216k inodes)** that are never pruned.

## Users

- **Herdr TUI panes / pi agents** — the heaviest spawners; every 30–60 s tick pays full process boot even for cache hits.
  - *As a herdr pane, I want cache-hit refreshes to cost near bare-node boot, so refresh cycles stop stealing core-seconds from the host.*
- **Operators / agents running ad-hoc `wl` commands** — every `wl create/update/comment/sync/next` pays the same boot cost.
  - *As an operator, I want `wl` commands to feel instant, so interactive and agent-driven use stops producing CPU bursts.*
- **Host administrators** — transient process bursts and an unbounded 890 MB cache dir degrade a shared Raspberry Pi / herdr server.
  - *As an admin, I want spawn load and cache disk bounded, so the host stays responsive.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- **(AC1)** **Import budget on the fast path:** the cache-hit read path and `--version` must not load command modules, the DB runtime, or plugins. Measured on the reference host (this repo, node ≥ 20): p95 wall time for a warm repeated `wl next --json` / `list --status open --json` cache hit ≤ **0.5 s** and peak RSS ≤ **60 MB** (current: ~0.6–1.2 s / 80–160 MB; bare node 0.35 s / 58 MB — the margin is deliberately tiny, so the fast-path import set must be slimmer than today's `read-cache-cli` graph at 61 MB). Enforced by a regression benchmark/test (e.g. asserts the heavy modules are not imported on the fast path).
- **(AC2)** **Measurable spawn-load reduction:** total CPU-seconds per 30 s refresh cycle across ≥ 4 panes on one shared worklog dir drops **≥ 60 %** versus current behaviour, measured by extending the env-gated spawn instrumentation (`WL_SPAWN_COUNT_FILE`, src/spawn-counter.ts) to record per-process CPU time (`process.resourceUsage().user+system`); baseline and after numbers quoted in the work item.
- **(AC3)** **Cache hygiene / bounded on-disk state:** `~/.cache/wl/state/` (216,228 files, ~890 MB, one file per worklog dir ever seen) is bounded and prunable — after a run, state storage is capped (bounded file count, or consolidated storage) and stale entries are removed; a documented maintenance path (`wl doctor cache` or automatic pruning) reclaims it. Freshness semantics unchanged (no correctness regression).
- **(AC4)** **No correctness regression:** all read-cache invariants from WL-0MSAZQEQB008O7H3 hold — write→read freshness, arg-variant separation, WAL-aware invalidation, concurrent readers/writers, byte-identical JSON for identical (dir, argv, version). The existing read-cache/e2e/spawn-reduction suites pass unchanged.
- **(AC5)** **Graceful degradation:** if lazy loading or the split entry point fails for any command, behaviour falls back to today's fully-registered CLI (no functional regression, help/plugin registration intact).
- **(AC6)** **Tests + docs:** unit/integration/benchmark tests cover the fast path, lazy loading, CPU-time instrumentation and cache hygiene; related documentation (CLI.md / CONFIG.md / docs as appropriate) updated; full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- **Stateless one-shot CLI** — no daemon, no long-lived server, no IPC worker (operator decision, Q1-A). Architecture and on-disk Git/JSONL sync semantics must not change.
- `wl` must keep working from any worktree/`--worklog-dir` (the prefix-to-sibling resolution and worklog-dir override must not be disturbed by splitting the entry point).
- Cache correctness invariants (WAL aware, TTL 30 s, LRU bound) are **non-negotiable** — the fast path only shortens import time.
- Node ESM, build via `tsc` to `dist/`; `/usr/local/bin/wl` symlinks into this repo's `dist/cli.js` (v1.0.22) — keep that contract intact.
- Performance benchmarks must be CPU-time based / tolerant on shared hosts (a Raspberry Pi, herdr server).

## Existing state

- Read-cache epic **shipped (WL-0MSAZQEQB008O7H3, v1.0.9)**: identical JSON reads (list/next/show/search/status) served pre-parse from `~/.cache/wl` with 83 % read-work reduction, sync+heartbeat, herdr in-process memoisation. Its audit records the accepted variance: "each invocation still spawns a wl process that exits without DB work" — the spawn itself was left in scope.
- pi-extension poll gating shipped (WL-0MSB1N0HB0007N6N + tests WL-0MSB446N4009FFT5); orphaned worktree process lifecycle shipped (WL-0MRP1SLZB005ZNYO).
- Herdr cadence: 30 s refresh × 4–5 wl fetches per pane, 60 s auto-sync with 45 s cross-instance heartbeat (packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts).
- Measured here: `node -e ''` 0.35 s/58 MB; `wl --version` 0.95 s/80 MB; `wl list --json` (repeated) 0.6–1.2 s/80–160 MB; `wl status` 1.74 s/180 MB; `wl sync --if-idle` 1.39 s/116 MB; importing `dist/cli-utils.js` alone 0.60 s/73 MB; `dist/read-cache-cli.js` 0.46 s/61 MB.

## Desired change

1. **Split the entry point:** keep `src/cli.ts` thin — argv scan + read-cache fast path (imports only `read-cache-cli`, `spawn-counter`, `worklog-paths` + minimal utils), then **dynamically import** the current heavy graph (`./cli-main.ts` or lazy command map). Cache hits and `--version` exit before commander/DB/plugins load.
2. **Lazy per-command imports:** replace the 35 eager `import XCommand` lines with a registry resolving each command on demand; `--help` / bare invocation may load all (rare).
3. **Extend spawn instrumentation** with per-process CPU time (ru_utime/ru_stime) to measure CPU-second reduction, not just spawn count.
4. **Cache hygiene:** bound/prune `~/.cache/wl/state/` (e.g. LRU/TTL over counter files, consolidate counters, housekeeping in `wl doctor`); optionally tidy stale top-level entries.
5. **If ≥60 % CPU-second reduction is not reached by import slimming alone** (spawn count unchanged), coalesce repeated herdr reads into fewer wl invocations (still stateless, e.g. one batch query per refresh tick) — record which lever was needed.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/cli.ts` — split entry: 40 eager imports (lines ~6–47), cache fast path (~526–545) that currently runs only after the full graph loads.
- `src/read-cache-cli.ts` — cache lookup/backfill/invalidation orchestration; the fast-path import set.
- `src/read-cache.ts` — `state/` counter files (`stateCounterFilePath`/`bumpStateCounter`, ~157–200), purge/LRU, entry layout.
- `src/spawn-counter.ts` — extend `SpawnRecord` with CPU time.
- `src/commands/*.ts` — command modules to lazy-load (next, list, status, show, search, sync, …).
- `src/plugin-loader.ts`, `src/cli-utils.ts`, `src/lib/runtime.ts` — heavy imports to defer.
- `src/commands/doctor.ts` — cache maintenance command (state pruning).
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — coalescing repeated reads per refresh tick (only if needed to hit AC2).
- Tests: `tests/read-cache.test.ts`, `tests/read-cache-cli.test.ts`, `tests/cli/read-cache-e2e.test.ts`, `tests/cli/read-cache-spawn-reduction.test.ts`, new `tests/cli/startup-import-budget.test.ts` / CPU-time benchmark.

## Related work

- **WL-0MSB19J56006E87J (completed, v1.0.7) — "Investigate excessive wl process spawning (206 concurrent, ~17 GB RAM)"** — the predecessor investigation. It attacked spawn *count* (pi browse-widget idle-gating → WL-0MSB1N0HB0007N6N, herdr cadence, read-cache). **Not a duplicate:** it left per-invocation *cost* and on-disk cache hygiene untouched; this item targets boot cost + `state/` growth.
- WL-0MSAZQEQB008O7H3 (completed) — read-cache epic; the spawn cost was its accepted variance; this item continues from there.
- WL-0MSB1N0HB0007N6N / WL-0MSB446N4009FFT5 (completed) — visibility-gated polling in pi extension / herdr (spawn-count side).
- WL-0MRP1SLZB005ZNYO (completed) — orphaned node process lifecycle in worktrees.
- WL-0MRTSPLAX005Y8QY (completed) — process lifecycle documentation (reference for docs conventions).
- WL-0MULOZ37S007VV13 (completed) — metrics collection module (host metric collection precedent; candidate to reuse for CPU-second reporting).
- WL-0MUAD8U24001ZK5K (completed) — `wl sync` before refactor/standup skills (lock-aware `sync --if-idle` spawners).
- Duplicate check performed — no overlapping open/in-progress item targeting wl startup cost; `WL-0MSB19J56006E87J` covers the already-shipped spawn-count remediation only.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Lazy/help registration risk:** commander help and plugin registration must not regress — mitigated by AC5 fallback and deferring full registration to the heavy path.
- **Entry-point tests:** several suites import `src/cli.ts` / `dist/cli.js` directly; splitting must keep those contracts (tests/cli/cli-inproc.ts, inproc-harness, smoke, completion, …).
- **Benchmark flakiness** on shared hosts — AC1/AC2 measured by CPU time, p95 over repeated runs, generous margins above bare-node baseline.
- **State-dir pruning races:** pruning counters concurrently with writers must stay atomic (temp+rename, no regression of counter monotonicity).
- **Scope-creep guard:** daemon/server mode, JSONL/Git sync changes, and TUI redesign are explicitly out of scope — recorded as related opportunities, not work here.
- **Assumption:** the reference-host measurements above are representative of the failing hosts (same repo/worklog versions; herdr panes are the dominant spawner).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 — "What's the target shape of the improvement?" — Answer (rgardler): **A — keep `wl` a stateless one-shot CLI; lazy per-command imports, fast path for cache hits/`--version` at near-node-boot cost, plus cache hygiene (prune `state/`, bound growth). No daemon.** Source: interactive reply.
- Q2 — "How should we measure success?" — Answer (rgardler): **A — total CPU-seconds per refresh cycle ≥ 60 % reduction; per-process RSS < 60 MB; no correctness regression.** Source: interactive reply.
- Research summary: measured per-invocation cost (0.6–1.7 s / 80–180 MB vs 0.35 s / 58 MB bare node), attributed to eager 40-module import graph; verified the read-cache fast path still loads the full graph before serving (src/cli.ts); confirmed unbounded `~/.cache/wl/state/` (216,228 files / ~890 MB) with no pruning path.

Phasing is vertical slices (tracer bullets): measurement first, then the entry-point fast path, then cache hygiene, then the CPU-second verdict and docs. Each slice covers its own code, tests and docs; between phases, review the next items' descriptions and re-check the measured numbers.

### Plan-stage decisions (recorded assumptions)

- **D1 — Budget enforcement is a ratchet, not a single hard-coded threshold.** AC1's 0.5 s / 60 MB budget is tighter than today's fast-path graph (0.46 s / 61 MB), so F2 checks in a budget file (`bench/startup-import-budget.json`) that records the statically reachable graph and the measured cost, and fails on growth. # F9 — Bound and prune the cache state directory via `wl doctor cache`

Implements desired change #4 and parent AC3: make the per-worklog-dir state counters a bounded, prunable on-disk store with a documented maintenance path, without touching freshness semantics.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Opportunistic pruning on cache writes keeps `state/` at or under a configured bound (default file count around 1,000 plus a TTL for untouched counters, aligned with the existing entry TTL/LRU). Measured on the reference host: a pre-populated 200k-file `state/` is reduced to the bound by one prune run, with file count, inode count and bytes quoted before and after in a comment.
- `wl doctor cache` exists with `--json`, a dry-run (report-only) mode and a prune mode. It reports file count, total bytes, stale-by-TTL count and live-dir count, and reclaims space when pruning. Bare `wl doctor` mentions pending cache state.
- Pruning is atomic and concurrency-safe (temp+rename, never truncating a live counter mid-write) and never deletes a counter whose worklog dir still has fresh cache entries; if entries exist, they are invalidated before the counter is dropped.
- Freshness correctness intact: the read-cache suites pass unchanged (parent AC4) and no stale read is served because a counter was pruned.
- The cap is configurable (env var or config key) with defaults safe on a Raspberry Pi class host, and the default is documented.
- Covers parent AC3: `~/.cache/wl/state/` is bounded and prunable — state storage is capped or consolidated, stale entries are removed, and a documented maintenance path (`wl doctor cache` or automatic pruning) reclaims it, with freshness semantics unchanged.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Add `pruneStateDir(cacheDir, { maxFiles, ttlMs, dryRun })` returning counts and bytes reclaimed.
2. Call it opportunistically and rate-limited (for example at most once per N minutes per process) from the cache write path, so growth is bounded without a daemon.
3. Add the `wl doctor cache` subcommand wiring the same function, reporting in text and `--json`.

**Key Files:**
- `src/read-cache.ts`
- `src/commands/doctor.ts`
- `src/read-cache-cli.ts`
- `CLI.md`
- `CONFIG.md`

## Dependencies

# Pi extension not showing work item title (WL-0MVGB23MM004X501)

## Problem statement

The Worklog Pi extension's footer shows the work item **ID** but silently omits the
**title** for some work items. The title is never displayed even though the
raw command text is shown, so the footer lacks the at-a-glance identification the
feature was built for (WL-0MQLG8PK80041FM3 / WL-0MQLJU82A000AT2W).

## Users

- **Pi TUI users** running Worklog skills with a work item ID.
  - *As a developer running `/intake RISE-0MVCFSM9B0019M8L`, I want the footer to
    show `intake RISE-0MVCFSM9B0019M8L AI cards should be face down` so I can
    confirm which item the agent is working on without scrolling the transcript.*
- **Herdr downtime workers** that auto-dispatch `/skill:intake` on cross-project
  items; their panes surface the same footer.

## Observed behaviour

- Footer always shows the work item ID.
- The title suffix is missing for *some* items only — the same command against a
  local project item shows both ID and title.
- Reproduced example from the report: `/intake RISE-0MVCFSM9B0019M8L`.

## Root-cause analysis (performed during intake)

Two independent failure modes share one symptom. Both are in the title-resolution
path used by the extension and are silent by design (the feature spec requires
graceful fallback with no error shown).

1. **Cross-project IDs are not resolved (primary).** Both title-resolution call
   sites spawn the CLI as `wl show <id> --json` with **cwd only**:
   - `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/activity-indicator.ts` →
     `resolveWorkItemTitle()` → `runWl('show', [id], { timeout: 2000 })`
   - `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/session-health.ts` → `startTicker()` →
     `runWl('show', [wlId], { timeout: 2000 })`

   `runWl` (`packages/tui/extensions/wl-integration.ts`) forwards to
   `runWlCommand` (`src/wl-integration/spawn.ts`), which spawns `wl` in
   `process.cwd()` and never passes `--worklog-dir`. Verified evidence:

   ```
   $ cd /home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub && wl show RISE-0MVCFSM9B0019M8L --json
   {"success": false, "error": "Work item not found: RISE-0MVCFSM9B0019M8L"}

   $ cd /home/rgardler/projects/tce-the-rising && wl show RISE-0MVCFSM9B0019M8L --json
   {"success": true, "workItem": {"id": "RISE-0MVCFSM9B0019M8L", "title": "AI cards should be face down", ...}}
   ```

   The skills layer *does* handle this — `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py`
   resolves `--worklog-dir` via a **prefix-to-sibling scan**
   (`SIBLING_SCAN_ROOT/*/.worklog/config.yaml`, `prefix: RISE` →
   `/home/rgardler/projects/tce-the-rising/.worklog`). The extension has no
   equivalent, so any ID whose prefix belongs to a sibling project silently
   falls back to raw text. A git-history scan (`git log -S "worklog-dir" --
   packages/tui/extensions/wl-integration.ts`) shows this gap is long-standing,
   not a recent regression — the feature only *appears* to "have stopped"
   working because cross-project work is now routine.

2. **The 2 s timeout is marginal for large items (secondary).** Measured on the
   reported example: cold run **2.36 s**, warm runs 1.10–1.29 s against an 18 KB
   JSON payload (full description). Local medium-size items measured
   1.15–1.29 s. Under machine load (concurrent agents/tests) a warm lookup can
   cross the 2 000 ms ceiling, so the same item can intermittently lose its
   title. This also explains the "doesn't always happen" phrasing.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When the footer resolves a work item ID that lives in a **sibling project's**
   worklog (e.g. `RISE-…` while the session cwd is ContextHub), the footer shows
   the command, the ID, and the resolved title — verified against the reported
   reproduction (`RISE-0MVCFSM9B0019M8L` → `AI cards should be face down`).
2. Title resolution uses the same prefix-to-sibling worklog resolution that the
   skills layer already uses (`prefix: <PFX>` in `SIBLING_SCAN_ROOT/*/.worklog/config.yaml`),
   falling back to cwd when no sibling matches — no new resolution algorithm is
   invented.
3. The same fix applies to **both** call sites: the activity-indicator status
   line (`activity-indicator.ts`) and the footer's initial-prompt preview
   (`session-health.ts`); a single shared resolver is used so they cannot drift.
4. The lookup timeout is raised (or the lookup made demonstrably fast enough)
   so that a large work item's title resolves reliably on a loaded machine; a
   regression test pins the timeout budget and a measured cold-start lookup for
   a >15 KB item succeeds.
5. Lookup failure still degrades silently to the raw text, displaying no error
   (preserves AC 3 of WL-0MQLG8PK80041FM3).
6. No new subprocess is spawned per keystroke/tick: sibling-prefix resolution is
   memoised per process (matching the memoised scan in `status_lifecycle.py`), so
   the per-tick footer refresh does not repeatedly scan the filesystem.
7. Regression tests cover: cross-project resolution success, unresolvable ID
   fallback, non-TUI mode degradation, and both call sites sharing the resolver.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
9. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- No change to `wl` CLI behaviour; the fix must live in the extension layer.
- `wl-integration.ts` must keep its existing `runWl(command, args, options)`
  signature working for all other callers (browse/lease/recovery modules).
- Prefix-to-sibling resolution must not shell out; read `.worklog/config.yaml`
  files directly, mirroring `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py`
  (`_find_worklog_dir_by_prefix`).
- Must degrade gracefully when `SIBLING_SCAN_ROOT` does not exist or a project's
  `config.yaml` is malformed (skip that project).
- Windows/portable: use `path` APIs, no shell globbing.
- Work item IDs follow `<PREFIX>-<HASH>` with a 2–3 letter uppercase prefix;
  the existing `WORK_ITEM_ID_REGEX` stays unchanged.

## Existing state

- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/activity-indicator.ts` — `resolveWorkItemTitle()`
  calls `runWl('show', [id], { timeout: 2000 })` with no worklog dir;
  `showActivityWithTitleLookup()` composes `${commandCtx} ${truncateWorkItemId(id)} ${title}`.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/session-health.ts` — `startTicker().refreshState()`
  enriches `state.initialPrompt` with the same `runWl('show', …, { timeout: 2000 })` call.
- `packages/tui/extensions/wl-integration.ts` — thin `runWl` wrapper that forwards
  `cwd`/`timeout` to `runWlCommand`; no worklog-dir awareness.
- `src/wl-integration/spawn.ts` — `runWlCommand(cmdArgs, { timeoutMs, cwd, env })`
  spawns `wl` in `cwd` with a default 15 s timeout and `maxBuffer` 20 MB.
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — reference implementation of
  prefix-to-sibling resolution (`SIBLING_SCAN_ROOT`, `_find_worklog_dir_by_prefix`,
  `functools.cache`-memoised).
- `tests/verify-blessed-removal.test.ts` only asserts the file exists; the
  original `activity-indicator.test.ts` was deleted in commit `386ba9a2`
  (WL-0MSGI7PV9004UD0N), so there is currently **no behavioural test** covering
  title resolution.

## Desired change

1. Add a shared, memoised worklog-dir resolver in the extension layer
   (e.g. `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/worklog-dir.ts`) that:
   - extracts the ID prefix (`^[A-Z]{2,3}-`),
   - scans `<SIBLING_SCAN_ROOT>/*/.worklog/config.yaml` for a matching `prefix:`,
   - caches the prefix→dir mapping for the process lifetime,
   - returns `null` when nothing matches (caller then falls back to cwd).
2. Extend `runWl` (or a dedicated `runWlForWorkItem`) to append
   `--worklog-dir <resolved>` when the command's args contain a work item ID.
3. Route both title-resolution call sites through that single helper; remove the
   duplicated `runWl('show', …)` blocks.
4. Raise the lookup budget (e.g. 5 s) *and* verify latency headroom in a test, so
   the footer still degrades gracefully but no longer times out on a large item
   on a warm DB.
5. Reinstate behavioural tests for `detectWorkItemId`, `formatCommandContext`,
   cross-project resolution, fallback-on-failure, and the shared resolver's
   memoisation.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/worklog-dir.ts` (new) — memoised
  prefix-to-sibling worklog-dir resolver (ported from `status_lifecycle.py`).
- `packages/tui/extensions/wl-integration.ts` — inject `--worklog-dir` for
  work-item-scoped commands; export the resolver for reuse.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/activity-indicator.ts` — use the shared
  resolver/helper in `resolveWorkItemTitle`; raise the timeout.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/session-health.ts` — same helper in
  `refreshState()`; delete the duplicated enrichment block.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/worklog-dir.test.ts` (new) — resolver:
  prefix hit, prefix miss, missing scan root, malformed config, memoisation.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/activity-indicator.test.ts` (restored) —
  title resolution, cross-project path, fallback, non-TUI degradation.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/session-health.test.ts` — initial-prompt
  enrichment uses the shared resolver.
- `README.md` / extension docs — note that cross-project IDs resolve via the
  sibling scan.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** `SIBLING_SCAN_ROOT` for the extension is the parent of the repo
  root (`/home/rgardler/projects`), matching `status_lifecycle.REPO_ROOT.parent`.
  The extension must derive it from its own installed location, not from
  `process.cwd()`; when it cannot be derived, resolution falls back to cwd
  (today's behaviour) rather than throwing.
- **Assumption:** the reported "footer" means both the line-1 activity status and
  the line-3 initial-prompt preview; the intake fix covers both since they share
  the same broken lookup.
- **Risk — starting a regression for in-repo IDs.** Passing `--worklog-dir`
  unconditionally could break worktree sessions, where `.worklog/` holds only a
  committed `config.yaml`. Mitigation: only pass the flag when a sibling prefix
  match is found, and keep cwd resolution otherwise; add a worktree test case.
- **Risk — filesystem scan cost per tick.** Mitigated by process-lifetime
  memoisation (AC 6) and by only scanning on a resolver cache miss.
- **Risk — test flakiness on timing.** The latency assertion (AC 4) could be
  environment-sensitive; pin it as a generous upper bound (e.g. ≤5 s) or measure
  the resolver's own budget rather than wall clock on a shared machine.
- **Scope-creep watch (linked follow-ups, not part of this change):** caching
  titles in the footer across sessions; showing status/priority in the footer;
  resolving multiple IDs in one command; surfacing a "not found" hint on
  failure. Record as separate work items if wanted.
- **Interpretation of "has stopped":** git history shows no regression — the
  cross-project gap predates the feature's original implementation. Documented
  here so the fix is not mis-scoped as a revert.

## Related work

- **WL-0MQLG8PK80041FM3** — Resolve work item IDs to titles in activity indicator
  footer (completed): introduced the resolution path and its graceful-fallback AC.
- **WL-0MQLJU82A000AT2W** — Preserve command context when showing resolved work
  item title in activity footer (completed): introduced `{command} {id} {title}`.
- **WL-0MRFH8W4J007HIY5** — Fix extractInitialPrompt to handle Pi's array-based
  content format (completed): added the line-3 initial-prompt title enrichment.
- **WL-0MUL1BG09005VRBO** — stale-ctx hardening of async paths (completed):
  guarded the post-await `showActivity` call; behaviour-neutral for this bug.
- **WL-0MRFOJFVA003S8IB** — Compact footer status line (completed): introduced
  `truncateWorkItemId` used in the composed footer label.
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — reference prefix-to-sibling resolver.
- `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — worklog-dir resolution
  background.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

### Original report (verbatim, producer)

> The Pi extension has stopped showing the item title in the footer. This doesn't
> always happen, only with some work items. It always shows the work item ID, but
> it should show the footer too. For example: /intake RISE-0MVCFSM9B0019M8L

No interview round was required: the report names the surface (footer), the
symptom (ID shown, title absent), and a concrete reproduction (`RISE-…`), and the
repo/CLI investigation below resolved the cause without needing producer input.

- **Q (interpretation, not asked):** does "it should show the footer too" mean
  the title should also appear? — **Assumed answer:** yes; the observed symptom is
  that the ID appears without the title, so the missing artefact is the title.
  Source: report text + reproduction. Status: **OPEN QUESTION** — see Research
  notes; the producer should confirm during review.

### Research notes

- **Duplicate check:** `wl search "Pi extension footer title"` and
  `wl search "extension title"` were run. The three completed items above overlap
  on the *feature* but none covers cross-project resolution or the timeout — this
  item is scoped to the gap, not a duplicate. No overlapping **open** item found.
- **Reproduction evidence:** `wl show RISE-0MVCFSM9B0019M8L --json` fails with
  "Work item not found" from ContextHub and succeeds from `tce-the-rising`.
  `tce-the-rising/.worklog/config.yaml` contains `prefix: RISE`.
- **Latency evidence:** cold `wl show RISE-0MVCFSM9B0019M8L --json` took 2.36 s
  for an 18 477-byte payload (budget in code: 2 000 ms); warm runs 1.10–1.29 s.
- **Git archaeology:** `git log -S "worklog-dir" -- packages/tui/extensions/wl-integration.ts`
  returns nothing — the extension never passed a worklog dir. Commit `9bc24414`
  (stale-ctx hardening) only wrapped the post-await call in `try/catch` and is
  behaviour-neutral. Commit `386ba9a2` deleted `activity-indicator.test.ts`,
  leaving the resolution path untested.
- **Open question (for producer review):** the report's phrase "it should show
  the footer too" is ambiguous — this brief assumes it means the **title** should
  also appear, which matches the observed symptom (ID shown, title absent). If
  the producer meant something else (e.g. a specific footer line disappearing),
  the diagnosis should be revisited.

## One-line headline summary

Work-item title resolution in the Pi extension footer silently fails for IDs that
live in a sibling project's worklog (e.g. `RISE-…`) and can time out on large
items; fix it by reusing the skills layer's prefix-to-sibling worklog resolution
in a single shared, memoised resolver for both footer call sites.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MRMG8P2X004V6YC** – help line for chord commands too verbose (completed)
- **WL-0MTF5WNRB009RHRU** – Pane-title: ID survives truncation, drop 'triggered' (completed)
- **WL-0MRDRZ32L00404D0** – Session Health Extension for Pi Footer (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: always, example, extension, footer, happen (+7 more)
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: always, extension, footer, happen, intake (+5 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: always, example, extension, happen, intake (+5 more)

# Validate that an operator dispatch from the herdr selection list gets higher priority

## Problem statement

Herdr's interactive dispatch path was built to send an operator-dispatched
work item's priority to the LLM proxy as a per-request `X-Priority` header
(parent epic WL-0MVE1NZ4J000H5NH), so that anything the operator actively
dispatches outranks unattended background work. The mapping functions, the
argument builder and the Pi extension are individually unit-tested, but there
is **no validation of the end-to-end interactive dispatch chain**: from an
operator invoking a dispatch on a selected work item in the herdr worklist,
through priority resolution and the `--request-priority` /
`HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY` plumbing, to the `X-Priority` header the proxy
receives. In particular `resolveInteractiveDispatchPriority` — the seam that
turns the dispatched command's work-item id into the interactive priority —
has no direct test. This item validates that the operator-dispatch path
really delivers the higher priority end to end, and fixes any gap found.

## Users

- **Agent operator (producer/developer)** running the herdr worklist — wants
  confidence that an interactive dispatch of a selected item gets routed
  ahead of background work by the proxy.

### Example user stories

- As an operator, when I dispatch a `medium`/`high`/`critical` item from the
  herdr selection list, its requests are served at `X-Priority: high` so they
  skip the contention queue.
- As an operator, when I dispatch an item with no resolvable id (free-form
  `/prompt:`), the dispatch still proceeds with the interactive default
  `high` (fail-open).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Integration test covers the interactive operator-dispatch path.** A test
   drives the seam `resolveInteractiveDispatchPriority(commandId, lookup)`
   (as wired in `index.ts` `onCommand`, i.e. `extractWorkItemId(command)` →
   `wl show` lookup → interactive mapping) and asserts the mapped request
   priority for the operator-dispatched work item, including the fail-open
   cases (absent id, lookup failure, timeout → `high`).
2. **End-to-end plumbing is pinned.** Tests assert that an operator dispatch
   whose work-item priority is `medium`/`high`/`critical`/`low` carries the
   corresponding interactive request priority (`high`/`high`/`high`/`medium`)
   through `buildSendToPiArgs(...)` (`--request-priority` flag) and into the
   launched process env (`HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY`), for both the pane and the
   headless `spawnBackgroundPi` paths.
3. **No regression in the fixed interactive mapping table.** The interactive
   table `low→medium`, `medium/high/critical→high`, unresolvable→`high`
   (fixed by parent AC2) is unchanged and its existing unit coverage still
   passes.
4. **Validation report.** Any discovered gap or fix (code or test) is recorded
   on the work item with commit hash; if no code change is needed beyond
   tests, the validation conclusion (operator dispatches carry higher
   priority) is recorded with the evidence.
5. **Testing criterion:** the changed-scope test gate (requires a test-first
   RED test demonstrating the gap before any fix) passes, and the full project
   test suite passes with the new changes.
6. **Documentation criterion:** all related documentation is updated to
   reflect the changes, including code comments, `packages/herdr/README.md`,
   and any relevant docs-site entries.

## Constraints

- **No changes to the proxy or the wire contract.** `X-Priority` with values
  `low|medium|high`, absent → proxy default `medium` (fixed by
  LP-0MVDT94F0003VHUA).
- **Fail-open is mandatory.** Priority resolution must never block or abort an
  interactive dispatch; unresolvable → interactive default `high`.
- The interactive mapping table is **fixed by the parent AC2** and must not be
  relaxed by this validation.
- Tests are run only through the standard test skill (`/skill:test`); no
  ad-hoc test invocation.
- Work lands on `dev` only, via the standard worktree/implement flow.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/request-priority.ts` — `mapInteractiveRequestPriority`,
  `mapDowntimeRequestPriority`, `resolveInteractiveRequestPriority`
  (fail-open; interactive default `high`). Fully unit-tested in
  `request-priority.test.ts` (parent children WL-0MVF3PYO3000EVJ3 /
  WL-0MVF3Q3VL000UNCN).
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `resolveInteractiveDispatchPriority`
  (line ~734, wraps `resolveInteractiveRequestPriority` +
  `lookupWorkItemPriority` via `wl show`); called in `onCommand` agent route
  (line ~2565) with `extractWorkItemId(command)`; priority forwarded via
  `buildSendToPiArgs` (`--request-priority`) and via env
  `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY` on the spawned `send-to-pi.sh` child and in
  `spawnBackgroundPi`. `buildSendToPiArgs`/`spawnBackgroundPi` priority
  behaviour is pinned in `index.test.ts` (WL-0MVF3PYO3000EVJ3 AC3/AC4), but
  `resolveInteractiveDispatchPriority` itself has **no direct test**.
- `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh` — accepts `--request-priority`,
  injects `exec env HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY=…` into the pane process.
  Not covered by an automated test.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/request-priority.ts` + test — Pi extension
  sets `X-Priority` via `before_provider_headers` from
  `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY`, fail-open (parent children WL-0MVF3Q2YC003RJPF /
  WL-0MVF3PZNY003413F).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` + `downtime-worker.priority.test.ts`
  — downtime dispatch env plumbing (tested; out of scope except as reference).

## Desired change

- Add the missing integration-level validation: a RED test-first spec driving
  `resolveInteractiveDispatchPriority` and the end-to-end arg/env plumbing for
  the interactive (operator) dispatch path, then any minimal implementation
  needed to make it pass (expected: none beyond wiring, if the code already
  behaves).
- If a genuine functional gap is found (e.g. a dispatch path that drops the
  priority), fix it minimally within the interactive-priority scope and pin it
  with a test; record the finding.
- Record the validation conclusion and evidence on the work item.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/request-priority.ts` — read-only reference; the mapping
  functions under validation.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `resolveInteractiveDispatchPriority`,
  `lookupWorkItemPriority`, `buildSendToPiArgs`, `onCommand` agent route
  (the seam being validated; minimal fix site if a gap is found).
- `packages/herdr/src/index.test.ts` — add the integration-level validation
  specs next to the existing `buildSendToPiArgs`/
  `spawnBackgroundPi` priority specs.
- `packages/herdr/src/request-priority.test.ts` — existing unit table
  coverage (must remain green).
- `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh` — `--request-priority` /
  `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY` injection (verification target; shell-level
  validation if within scope).
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — documentation if a caveat/assumption needs
  recording.

## Related work

- **WL-0MVE1NZ4J000H5NH** (completed/in_review, parent) — "Remove fast/cheap
  mode switches, replace with priority on requests"; AC2 fixes the interactive
  mapping table this item validates.
- **WL-0MVF3Q3VL000UNCN** (completed) — Interactive dispatch request priority
  (implementation of the path under validation).
- **WL-0MVF3PYO3000EVJ3** (completed) — Tests: priority mapping & interactive
  dispatch (existing unit-level specs).
- **WL-0MVF3Q2YC003RJPF** / **WL-0MVF3PZNY003413F** (completed) — Pi extension
  `X-Priority` header injection and its tests.
- **WL-0MVF3Q4X5001FOXV** (completed) — Downtime dispatch request priority
  (reference for the parallel downtime path).
- **LP-0MVDT94F0003VHUA** (`llm-manager`, completed) — proxy-side priority
  routing (`X-Priority` contract).
- Duplicate check performed — no completed item found that already validates
  the operator-dispatch interactive priority end to end; this item is not a
  duplicate.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — validation reveals a real behavioural gap.** If a dispatch path
  drops the priority, scope is limited to the interactive operator path;
  anything broader is recorded as a new linked work item, not added here.
- **Risk — shell-level (`send-to-pi.sh`) validation is heavyweight.** The
  env-injection behaviour is partially covered transitively by the
  arg/env specs; explicit shell-level validation is included only if it is
  cheap and non-flaky, otherwise the finding is documented instead.
- **Assumption — the intended deliverable is automated integration-test
  validation plus a recorded conclusion**, not a change to the mapping
  contract (fixed by the parent).
- **Scope-creep guard:** downtime dispatch (already tested), proxy-side
  changes, and trust-gate hardening (LP-0MVDTE0CI0088QOR) are out of scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- No clarifying questions were required: the seed context ("validate that an
  operator dispatch from the herdr selection list is sent as higher priority
  so the proxy routes it") combined with the completed parent epic and
  existing unit coverage makes the deliverable unambiguous — validate the
  interactive operator-dispatch chain end to end and fix/pin any gap with
  tests. Assumption recorded above: automated integration-test validation is
  the expected form of "validate".

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MLYHCZCS1FY5I6H** – wl next should not prefer blockers of lower-priority items over higher-priority open items (completed)
- **WL-0MM346ZBD1YSKKSV** – Blocker Priority Inheritance (completed)

- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: dispatches, gets, herdr, list, operator, plugin, priority, proxy, routes, selection, sent, should, validate, when

## Problem

`.pi/test-config.json` defines the full suite as `npm --silent test -- tests/cli` + `npm --silent test -- tests/unit`. The `packages/herdr/src/*.test.ts` suite (~3.4k tests) is therefore **never** run by the dev-push gate, the ship release gate, or `implement.py finish`, even though herdr work items (e.g. WL-0MVEDM8OT007WDRS AC6/AC8) require it.

Child sessions work around this by running `npm --silent test -- packages/herdr/src` ad hoc, which bypasses the test skill's sanctioned runner and cache (so audits cannot see the evidence), and means a red herdr tree can be pushed to `dev` undetected. `run_tests.py --type herdr` fails with an unknown-type error because no local test extension or group defines it.

## Desired change

2. Decide whether the herdr suite also joins the full gate (cost ~12-19 min) or stays a separate gate invoked by items that touch it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `python3 run_tests.py --type herdr --json` runs the herdr package suite and records a cache entry.
